literal: Wen Cheng's Five Sons, Xianwen's Six Sons, Xiaowen's Six Sons
idiomatic: Wen Cheng's Five Sons, Xianwen's Six Sons, Xiaowen's Six Sons

literal: Biographies 7
idiomatic: Biographies 7

literal: Wen Cheng's Five Sons, Xianwen's Six Sons, and Xiaowen's Six Sons
idiomatic: Wen Cheng's Five Sons, Xianwen's Six Sons, and Xiaowen's Six Sons

literal: Prince of Anle Chang Le, in the fourth year of Huangxing was enfeoffed Prince of Changchang; later he was reassigned Prince of Anle.
idiomatic: Chang Le, Prince of Anle, was enfeoffed as Prince of Changchang in the fourth year of Huangxing and later reassigned as Prince of Anle.

literal: Chang Le's nature was grave and steady; Xianwen prized and loved him.
idiomatic: Steady and grave by nature, Chang Le was a favorite of Xianwen.

literal: In the first year of Chengming he was appointed Grand Commandant and sent out as Governor of Ding Province.
idiomatic: In the first year of Chengming he became Grand Commandant and went out as Governor of Ding Province.

literal: He humiliated officials and many did not obey the law; the people went to the palace to sue him, and Xiaowen punished him with thirty strokes of the staff.
idiomatic: He abused officials and flouted the law until commoners petitioned at court; Xiaowen had him beaten thirty strokes with the staff.

literal: His greed and violence grew worse, and he was summoned to the capital on criminal charge.
idiomatic: His greed and cruelty deepened until he was summoned to the capital on criminal charge.

literal: Later he plotted rebellion; when the affair broke he was ordered to die at home, buried with princely rites, and given the posthumous name Stern.
idiomatic: He later plotted treason; when it was exposed he was ordered to die at home, buried with princely rites, and posthumously named Stern.

literal: His son Quan, styled Souxian, succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Quan, styled Souxian, inherited the title.

literal: At the start of Xuanwu's reign he was made Governor of Liang Province.
idiomatic: Early in Xuanwu's reign he was made Governor of Liang Province.

literal: In the province he was greedy and corrupt; government was bought with bribes.
idiomatic: In office he was greedy and corrupt; government ran on bribes.

literal: Later he was removed and made Governor of Ding Province.
idiomatic: He was later transferred to Governor of Ding Province.

literal: When Prince of Jingzhao Yu rebelled, Quan falsely announced that the state was in turmoil.
idiomatic: When the Prince of Jingzhao, Yu, rebelled, Quan spread word that the realm was in turmoil.

literal: The garrisons of the northern provinces all suspected trouble at court and sent envoys to watch Quan's movements.
idiomatic: Northern garrison commanders suspected upheaval at court and sent men to watch Quan.

literal: Quan reported the full situation, and the provinces and garrisons settled down.
idiomatic: Quan reported the facts in full, and the provinces and garrisons calmed.

literal: Yu fled to Xin Du; Quan with Li Ping, Gao Zhi, and others attacked from four sides and set fires; Yu burst through a gate and fled.
idiomatic: Yu fled to Xin Du; Quan, Li Ping, Gao Zhi, and others attacked from four sides with fire until Yu broke out through a gate and escaped.

literal: Soon after he was made Palace Attendant, and for his role in the first report he was also made Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the Left.
idiomatic: He was soon made Palace Attendant and, for leading the first report, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the Left.

literal: He died; his posthumous name was Wukang.
idiomatic: He died and was posthumously named Wukang.

literal: His son Jian, styled Changwen, succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Jian, styled Changwen, inherited the title.

literal: Later he was made Governor of Xiang Province and Grand Commander of the Northern Campaign to attack Ge Rong.
idiomatic: He was later made Governor of Xiang Province and Grand Commander of the Northern Campaign against Ge Rong.

literal: He also held Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the Left, Northern Route Mobile Office Director of the Masters of Writing, and with Commander Pei Yan jointly besieged Xin Du.
idiomatic: He also held the vice directorship on the left, directed the Northern Route mobile office, and with Commander Pei Yan besieged Xin Du.

literal: Jian was a mediocrity; seeing the realm in turmoil he plotted rebellion and surrendered to Ge Rong.
idiomatic: Mediocre in talent, Jian saw the realm in chaos and plotted rebellion, surrendering to Ge Rong.

literal: Commander Yuan Ziyong and Pei Yan jointly besieged Jian, beheaded him, and sent the head to Luoyang; an edict changed his surname to Yuan.
idiomatic: Commander Yuan Ziyong and Pei Yan besieged him, beheaded him, and sent the head to Luoyang; an edict changed his clan name to Yuan.

literal: At the start of Emperor Zhuang's reign his original clan was restored, and Jian's princely title was specially restored with posthumous gift of Minister of Works.
idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Zhuang's reign his clan was restored and Jian's princely title specially revived with posthumous rank as Minister of Works.

literal: Jian's younger brother Binzhi, styled Zishuang, was treacherous and without conduct.
idiomatic: Jian's younger brother Binzhi, styled Zishuang, was treacherous and without principle.

literal: When he rebelled with Jian and was defeated, he fled to Ge Rong.
idiomatic: When he joined Jian's rebellion and was defeated, he fled to Ge Rong.

literal: When Ge Rong was destroyed he was able to return.
idiomatic: After Ge Rong's destruction he returned.

literal: Under Emperor Xiaowu he was enfeoffed Prince of Yingchuan and entrusted with duties of intimate trust.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowu he was made Prince of Yingchuan and given duties of intimate trust.

literal: When the emperor entered Guanzhong, Binzhi fled to Liang.
idiomatic: When the emperor entered Guanzhong, Binzhi fled to Liang.

literal: In the second year of Datong he returned to Chang'an and held Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: In the second year of Datong he returned to Chang'an as Director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: He died; posthumous gift of Grand Commandant, posthumous name Wuxiang.
idiomatic: He died; posthumous gift of Grand Commandant and name Wuxiang.

literal: Prince of Guangchuan Lue, enfeoffed in the second year of Yanxing, held the office of Grand Director of the Palace at the Center.
idiomatic: The Prince of Guangchuan, Lue, enfeoffed in the second year of Yanxing, was Grand Director of the Palace at the Center.

literal: Clear and sharp by nature, in judging cases he was called fair.
idiomatic: Clear and sharp by nature, he was known for fair judgments.

literal: In the fourth year of Taihe he died.
idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Taihe.

literal: His posthumous name was Zhuang.
idiomatic: His posthumous name was Zhuang.

literal: His son Xie, styled Zhonghe, succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Xie, styled Zhonghe, inherited the title.

literal: In the nineteenth year he died.
idiomatic: He died in the nineteenth year.

literal: An edict said: "In antiquity at the death of great ministers there was the rite of three visits—this applied to those of rank Three Excellencies and above.
idiomatic: An edict said: "In antiquity great ministers received three imperial visits at death—this was for those of Three Excellencies rank and above.

literal: From Han downward many lacked this rite.
idiomatic: From Han onward the rite was often neglected.

literal: We wish to follow the ancient model in spirit and let grief move with feeling.
idiomatic: We wish to follow the ancient model and let grief answer feeling.

literal: Though rank requires restraint, private pain may not be denied.
idiomatic: Though rank demands restraint, private pain should not be denied.

literal: We wish princes with close kin in the first degree of mourning to make three visits, those in the second degree two visits, and those in the third and fifth degrees one visit.
idiomatic: Princes with first-degree mourning kin should make three visits, second-degree kin two, third- and fifth-degree kin one.

literal: The Prince of Guangchuan bears to Us mourning of the second degree; if he must have two visits, We wish to visit in person at the great encoffining to exhaust grief, and after assuming mourning garments to attend in fifth-degree hemp.
idiomatic: The Prince of Guangchuan is second-degree kin to Us; for two visits We would attend the great encoffining in person, then after assuming garments attend in fifth-degree hemp.

literal: Once the coffin is set, fifth-degree hemp is surely without doubt.
idiomatic: After the coffin is sealed, fifth-degree hemp is surely proper.

literal: As to the visit at great encoffining—is it fitting?
idiomatic: Is the visit at great encoffining fitting?

literal: Must one stroke the bier at the first mourning?
idiomatic: Must one stroke the bier at first mourning?

literal: Or should grief be exhausted at closing the coffin?
idiomatic: Or exhaust grief only when the coffin is closed?

literal: Huangmen Attendant Cui Guang, Song Bian, Regular Attendant Liu Fang, Lower Grandee of Orders Li Yuankai, Secretariat Attendant Gao Cong, and others deliberated: "The three visits are indeed ancient rite.
idiomatic: Cui Guang, Song Bian, Liu Fang, Li Yuankai, Gao Cong, and others said: "Three visits are ancient rite.

literal: Down through Han and Wei few practiced it;
idiomatic: Through Han and Wei few practiced it;

literal: Your Majesty now follows the former track.
idiomatic: Your Majesty now follows the former path.

literal: We deem that for first-degree kin three visits, for second-degree kin two are fitting.
idiomatic: For first-degree kin three visits, for second-degree kin two.

literal: At the start of mourning grief is utmost; since feeling lowers rank, one should follow the start of mourning.
idiomatic: At first mourning grief is utmost; since feeling tempers rank, follow the start of mourning.

literal: As to the visit at great encoffining, we submit to the sacred intent.
idiomatic: The visit at great encoffining we submit to Your Majesty's intent.

literal: An edict said: "From Wei and Jin onward personal visits were often lacking; for kin and ministers they were sure to weep in the Eastern Hall.
idiomatic: An edict said: "Since Wei and Jin, emperors often skipped personal visits; for kin and ministers they wept in the Eastern Hall.

literal: Recently when Grand Marshal the Prince of Anding died, after We visited him We received condolences in the Eastern Hall.
idiomatic: When Grand Marshal the Prince of Anding died, We visited him then received condolences in the Eastern Hall.

literal: For today's affair—should We weep again?
idiomatic: For today—should We weep again?

literal: Guang and others said: "Weeping in the Eastern Hall was because of not visiting in person.
idiomatic: They said: "Eastern Hall weeping was for lack of personal visit.

literal: Now Your Majesty personally attends; ministers follow the carriage—we deem further weeping unfitting.
idiomatic: Now Your Majesty attends in person and ministers follow—we deem further weeping unfitting.

literal: An edict said: "If the Grand Marshal is kin of weighty rank, he must be wept for in the Eastern Hall.
idiomatic: An edict said: "If the Grand Marshal is kin of weighty rank, Eastern Hall weeping is required.

literal: But the Prince of Guangchuan is a king's son and still young in years and rank—as you deliberate, We have no objection.
idiomatic: The Prince of Guangchuan is a king's son and young in years and rank—as you see fit, We agree.

literal: When Xie was about to be greatly encoffined, the emperor in plain dress and deep garments wept; entering the chamber he wailed bitterly, stroked the corpse, and went out.
idiomatic: At Xie's great encoffining the emperor wore plain dress and deep garments, entered wailing, stroked the corpse, and withdrew.

literal: Chen, styled Tanbao, was clever and perceptive as a child; Xiaowen loved him.
idiomatic: Chen, styled Tanbao, was clever and perceptive as a boy; Xiaowen loved him.

literal: Under Xuanwu he was made Governor of Ding Province.
idiomatic: Under Xuanwu he was made Governor of Ding Province.

literal: Chen's consort was Xuanwu's maternal niece, younger sister of Empress Gao.
idiomatic: His consort was Xuanwu's maternal niece, younger sister of Empress Gao.

literal: Relying on inside and outside connections, in the province he was greedy.
idiomatic: Relying on court and family ties, he was greedy in office.

literal: On returning to court Empress Ling said: "In Ding Province Chen brought everything except the Zhongshan palace—how can he be employed!
idiomatic: On return Empress Ling said: "In Ding he took everything but the Zhongshan palace—how employ him?

literal: Because of this he was dismissed to his home.
idiomatic: He was dismissed to his home.

literal: When Mingdi first studied, Chen presented a gold-letter Classic of Filial Piety.
idiomatic: When Mingdi began studies Chen presented a gold-letter Classic of Filial Piety.

literal: Unable to advance by his own means, he made Liu Teng his adoptive son and bribed Teng with gold and jewels in sums of tens of thousands.
idiomatic: Unable to advance on his own, he made Liu Teng his adoptive father and bribed him with gold and jewels beyond counting.

literal: Teng spoke for him and he obtained concurrent Director of the Ministry of Justice.
idiomatic: Teng spoke for him and he gained concurrent Director of the Ministry of Justice.

literal: Sent out as Governor of Qin Province, in the province he amassed wealth and the people groaned.
idiomatic: As Governor of Qin he amassed wealth until the people groaned.

literal: When the Di of Eastern Yi and Southern Qin rebelled, an edict made Chen mobile-office commander and also acting commander, returning to hold provincial affairs.
idiomatic: When Di of Eastern Yi and Southern Qin rebelled, he was made mobile-office commander and acting commander, resuming provincial duties.

literal: Holding both army and province, his desires knew no limit.
idiomatic: Commanding army and province, his appetites knew no limit.

literal: Advancing to attack Di and Qiang, he inflicted great defeats.
idiomatic: Attacking Di and Qiang he inflicted great defeats.

literal: Within he relied on Liu Teng and feared nothing.
idiomatic: Within he relied on Liu Teng and feared nothing.

literal: The Commandant of Justice impeached him; an amnesty came and he was struck from the rolls.
idiomatic: The Commandant of Justice impeached him; amnesty struck him from the rolls.

literal: Soon his princely title was restored.
idiomatic: Soon his princely title was restored.

literal: Later attacking Xianyu Xiuli he was defeated and stripped of office and title.
idiomatic: Later, attacking Xianyu Xiuli, he was defeated and stripped of office and title.

literal: Later attacking Hu of Fen and Jin and Shu, he died in the army; posthumously his princely title was restored.
idiomatic: Later, campaigning against Hu of Fen and Jin and Shu, he died in the army; his princely title was posthumously restored.

literal: Prince of Anfeng Meng, styled Jilie, was enfeoffed in the fifth year of Taihe and made Palace Attendant.
idiomatic: The Prince of Anfeng, Meng, styled Jilie, was enfeoffed in the fifth year of Taihe and made Palace Attendant.

literal: Sent out as Grand General of the Garrison Capital and Governor of Ying Province.
idiomatic: He was sent out as Grand General of the Garrison Capital and Governor of Ying Province.

literal: Meng was broad, benevolent, bold, and resolute, with great authority and strategy; the barbarians feared and loved him.
idiomatic: Broad, benevolent, bold, and resolute, he had great authority; barbarians feared and loved him.

literal: He died in the province; posthumous gift of Grand Commandant, posthumous name Kuang.
idiomatic: He died in office; posthumous gift of Grand Commandant and name Kuang.

literal: His son Yanming succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Yanming inherited the title.

literal: Under Xuanwu he was made Grand Palace Grandee.
idiomatic: Under Xuanwu he was made Grand Palace Grandee.

literal: At the start of Yan Chang, in a year of great famine, Yanming reduced family wealth to save several dozen guests and support their households.
idiomatic: In the first year of Yan Chang, a year of famine, he spent family wealth to save dozens of guests and their households.

literal: By the start of Mingdi he was Governor of Yu Province with marked achievements in government.
idiomatic: By Mingdi's accession he was Governor of Yu Province with marked achievements.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Attendant of the Yellow Gate within the Palace.
idiomatic: He rose to Attendant of the Yellow Gate within the Palace.

literal: Yanming had mastered the classics and also literary talent; he gathered more than ten thousand scrolls of books and maps.
idiomatic: He had mastered the classics and literary talent, gathering more than ten thousand scrolls.

literal: His nature was pure and frugal; he did not pursue estates.
idiomatic: Pure and frugal, he did not pursue estates.

literal: With the Prince of Zhongshan Xi and his younger brother the Prince of Linhuai Yu he shared literary renown famous in the age.
idiomatic: With the Prince of Zhongshan Xi and his brother the Prince of Linhuai Yu he shared literary fame.

literal: Though in casual elegance he did not match Xi and Yu, in classical learning and solid virtue he surpassed them.
idiomatic: In casual elegance he fell short of Xi and Yu; in classical learning and solid virtue he surpassed them.

literal: Promoted to Palace Attendant, an edict ordered him with Palace Attendant Cui Guang to fix mourning garments.
idiomatic: Promoted to Palace Attendant, he was ordered with Cui Guang to fix mourning garments.

literal: Later he also held Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the Right.
idiomatic: He later held Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the Right.

literal: Because Yanming was broadly learned, he was ordered to supervise metal and stone affairs.
idiomatic: For his broad learning he was ordered to supervise metal and stone inscriptions.

literal: When Yuan Faseng rebelled, an edict made him Eastern Route mobile office, Grand Commander of Xu Province, directing all military affairs.
idiomatic: When Yuan Faseng rebelled he was made Eastern Route mobile office and Grand Commander of Xu Province.

literal: With Commander the Prince of Linhuai Yu and Master of Writing Li Xian he attacked Faseng.
idiomatic: With the Prince of Linhuai Yu and Li Xian he attacked Faseng.

literal: Liang sent the Prince of Yuzhang Zong to garrison Xu Province.
idiomatic: Liang sent the Prince of Yuzhang Zong to garrison Xu Province.

literal: Yanming had earlier governed Xu region and won great praise of the people;
idiomatic: Yanming had earlier governed Xu and won the people's praise;
